title: implement init-rate-controller and configurable rollback-window for private installer
author: Maya Raghavan
description:
Motivation: private installs in large tenants can launch many tenant-init jobs concurrently during upgrades which overloads control-plane and shared storage (observed in SUP-8342). This PR adds a lightweight helm templated init-rate-controller (ConfigMap + CronJob-based reconciler) and a configurable cluster-level rollback_window to prevent rapid rollbacks during rolling upgrades.

Summary of changes: adds a values schema extension to define init rate and rollback window; introduces templates for init-rate-controller and rollback-watchdog with leader election fallback; updates _helpers.tpl with rate helper functions; adds a minimal migration hook to apply ConfigMap defaults during upgrades; includes unit helm chart tests and an example values file.

Checklist:
- [x] values schema & docs updated
- [x] templates for controller and watchdog implemented
- [x] helm lint & unit tests passing
- [x] migration hook for existing installs added
- [x] rollouts tested in QA cluster (staging-nyc)

Behavior:
- init.rateController.enabled: when true, installs a CronJob-based reconciler that observes tenant init Jobs (label: redwood.io/init-job) and patches active job concurrency via an init-rate ConfigMap. This is intentionally non-CRD to keep installer footprint small and airgap-friendly.
- init.rateController.globalMaxConcurrency: cluster-wide cap for concurrent tenant init Jobs. Per-tenant caps can be set via values or left to defaults.
- rollback.windowSeconds: when set > 0, the rollback-watchdog will prevent executing rollback hooks for the configured window after a successful upgrade to reduce churn from flapping upgrades.

Migration notes: the migration hook applies a namespaced ConfigMap for default rate limits; existing installs without the new values will have conservative defaults (globalMaxConcurrency=10, rollback.windowSeconds=300). The hook is idempotent.

Security & operational notes: the reconciler runs with a read-write ServiceAccount limited to patch/patch/status on Jobs in the release namespace and create/update ConfigMaps. RBAC rules are scoped by namespace for Private installs.

Why not a CRD: Introduced footprint + airgap distribution concerns and operator lifecycle overhead. A helm-managed CronJob reconciler is simpler to reason about in the Private installer context and fits our ops model for customers that prefer no cluster-wide operators.

review_comments: Oliver Chen: Can we avoid patching Jobs if the controller detects the cluster is under duress? Suggest adding a cheap API-based qps check before modifying job parallelism.

Maya Raghavan (author): Good point — added a soft qps probe and fallback no-op mode (configurable). See init-rate-controller-cronjob.yaml lines 40-78 where the reconciler checks /healthz of kube-apiserver and honors rateController.fallbackOnDuress.

Priya Patel: RBAC looks tight but we need a note in README for operators to grant namespace-level bind if they run installer with restricted RBAC. Also request an e2e smoke test in staging before merging.
Maya Raghavan (author): Added README note and a helm-unittest that simulates namespace missing patch permission; reconciler exits cleanly. Staging e2e was run on 2026-02-28 per PR pipeline results.
Samir Vasquez: rollback.windowSeconds semantics are fine, but we should ensure webhook-driven rollbacks (external tooling) still respect Window. Added a test suggestion to the docs.
Maya Raghavan (author): Added note: watchdog emits a ConfigMap flag (redwood.io/rollback-guard) that external tooling can read — documented in README and migration hook.
merge_details: Merged by Priya Patel using squash merge. Squash commit includes CHANGES.md section and migration note. Backported to release/2026-Q1 via PR #911157.
release_notes: Introduce optional init.rateController to limit concurrent tenant init jobs and a rollback.windowSeconds to throttle immediate rollbacks after upgrades. Defaults set conservatively; requires no manual action for default installs. See charts/redwood-private/README.md for configuration and migration steps.
notes_for_ops: Defaults: init.rateController.enabled=false, globalMaxConcurrency=10, rollback.windowSeconds=300. To enable in production, set init.rateController.enabled=true and tune globalMaxConcurrency to match control-plane capacity. Monitor metrics: redwood.initcontroller.active_jobs and redwood.rollback.watchdog_events.
testing_summary: Unit helm-unittest suite added (3 cases). Performed staged upgrade on staging-nyc with 120 tenant init jobs; controller reduced peak concurrent jobs from ~120 to target 10 and rollout completed with stable API QPS. No regressions in helm-lint or packaging.
